boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Rose-Hulman study environments, from quiet library seating to reservable rooms and academic support spaces.

cards.title: Logan Library Main-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: John A. Logan Library
cards.notes: Set up on the main floor when you want a library study area near the building’s coffee shop; bring headphones for a shared environment.
cards.short_summary: A large main-floor study area in the heart-of-campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s campus map states that Logan Library has a large study area on its main floor and a coffee shop.
cards.access_notes: Use during posted Logan Library hours; hours vary during holidays and breaks.

cards.title: Logan Library Upper-Level Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: John A. Logan Library, upper level
cards.notes: Choose the upper level for quiet work, then use the library’s research help or collections downstairs if your assignment needs sources.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s 2025 first-year guide identifies the upper level of Logan Library as quiet study space.
cards.source_title: Guide to Thrive: How to Navigate the First-Year
cards.access_notes: Library regular hours: Mon–Thu 7:45 a.m.–midnight; Fri 7:45 a.m.–5 p.m.; Sat 1–6 p.m.; Sun noon–midnight. Hours may vary.

cards.title: Logan Library Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: John A. Logan Library
cards.notes: Use this library computer option when you need a campus workstation rather than your own device; confirm availability with library staff.
cards.short_summary: A library study option with campus computer access.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s Logan Library orientation says students have access to a computer lab and quiet study space at the library.
cards.access_notes: Rose-Hulman identifies this as a student library resource; check current library hours before going.

cards.title: Logan Library Reservable Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: John A. Logan Library
cards.notes: Reserve a room for a focused project meeting or small-group review; select a room size that matches your group before you arrive.
cards.short_summary: Bookable library rooms for groups of two to 12 students.
cards.evidence_claim: Logan Library offers reservable study rooms seating two to 12 students, available on a first-come-first-served basis.
cards.access_notes: Room reservations are available for rooms seating two to 12 students; availability is first-come-first-served.

cards.title: Logan Library Reservable Conference Room
cards.subtitle: John A. Logan Library
cards.notes: Use the library’s reservable conference-room option when your project needs a dedicated shared table; reserve before planning around it.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated, bookable conference space in Logan Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman lists a reservable conference room among Logan Library’s first-come-first-served study spaces.
cards.access_notes: The library identifies the conference room as reservable and subject to first-come-first-served availability.

cards.title: Learning Center Quiet Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Lower level, John A. Logan Library
cards.notes: Pair a quiet-work session with tutoring or course materials when useful; the Learning Center serves both individual and small-group study.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study beside tutoring and review resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Center offers quiet study areas for individuals or small groups and is located in the lower level of Logan Library.
cards.access_notes: Tutors are available with or without appointment Mon–Fri 9 a.m.–4:50 p.m. and Sun–Thu 7–10 p.m.; verify current availability.

cards.title: Mathematics Casual Study Space
cards.subtitle: Department of Mathematics, Moench Hall
cards.notes: Bring your own coffee if you want the stated coffee-shop feel, then use the small tables, reference library, and whiteboard for problem sets.
cards.short_summary: A math-department space with tables, references, and a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s mathematics department describes its casual study space as having a coffee-shop atmosphere, small tables, a reference library, and a whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: The department describes the space as BYOC (bring your own coffee); confirm departmental access before relying on it.

cards.title: Waters Computer Center
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Crapo Hall
cards.notes: Head to the lower level of Crapo Hall when coursework calls for a computer-center setting; verify lab availability before planning a long session.
cards.short_summary: Campus computer-center space inside Crapo Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman identifies the Waters Computer Center as being in the lower level of Crapo Hall.
cards.access_notes: The official page identifies the location but does not publish public access rules or hours; confirm access locally.

cards.title: Engineering Learning Center Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: First-Year Engineering Program tutoring center
cards.notes: Use an individual room for a small engineering work session, taking advantage of the documented tables, chairs, whiteboards, and markers.
cards.short_summary: Individual rooms equipped for hands-on engineering collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: A Rose-Hulman conference paper describes Engineering Learning Center individual study rooms with tables, chairs, whiteboards, and markers.
cards.source_title: Development and Implementation of Escape Rooms for an Engineering Summer Bridge Program
cards.access_notes: This is a First-Year Engineering Program tutoring-center space; current access and room-use procedures are not published on the cited source.

cards.title: MRH Central Study Areas
cards.subtitle: New Residence Hall (MRH)
cards.notes: If you live in MRH, use its central study areas for a nearby session; observe residence-hall access and community-space expectations.
cards.short_summary: Central study space within Rose-Hulman’s newest residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s new residence hall page describes MRH as having central study areas and lounges, with the hall opened in fall 2025.
cards.access_notes: Located inside a residence hall; use is subject to residence-hall access and community-space rules.
